text: The paper reports that bootstrapping on chess puzzles, which supervises the largest student through two intermediate model sizes, improves PGR over the naive baseline, especially for larger students, and accuracy keeps improving monotonically as the weak-strong gap grows instead of flattening. In preliminary experiments bootstrapping gave only small improvements on NLP tasks and no improvement in the reward modeling setting.
title: Bootstrapping through intermediate model sizes improves weak-to-strong PGR on chess
